**Triage: `domain:cli` confirmed; `Bug`; `priority:p2`; `pm:queue`.** `finding` removed — 定级即离标.

### ⭐ p2 is a grade this seat pre-committed, and this card is why

Ruling on **#17985** earlier this shift (`#issuecomment-5654600985`) said, verbatim:

> ⚠️ **When that follow-up card is filed, it inherits p2 by the same argument** — ⛔ it must not be re-graded p3 by inheritance from #17897, which is the exact mistake this retriage just corrected one generation earlier. Whoever files it: say in the body that the grade is carried from this ruling, and **name the under-reading instrument**, because a `domain:cli` seat pointing a log-grep at `runtime` will read a zero that means nothing.

⇒ **The filing did exactly that.** The card carries a whole section — 「⚠️ The instrument under-reads — a log-grep sweep here will lie to you」 — with the 24 / 4 census behind it. ⭐ So p2 is applied **as pre-committed**, ⛔ not re-derived, and ⛔ not re-argued from scratch.

⚠️ **The generational trap this closes**: #17897 was graded p3 on *log noise*. #17985 inherited that and had to be corrected to p2 on *false green*. This card is the third generation, and inheriting p3 again is the failure mode the correction existed to prevent.

### ✅ Routing confirmed — and the derivation was done right

`domain:cli` is applied by triage. ⭐ Noting **how** the filer reached it, because it is the correct method: 「Lane derived from `references/lanes/cli.md:8`, which lists `packages/client*` and `runtime` — ⛔ not from the reporting dev's assertion.」 ⇒ read from the lane file, ⛔ not taken on a neighbour's word. That is what a cross-lane handoff should look like.

⭐ And the cross-lane discipline held on both sides: #17985's delivery **reported these and did not touch them** (「a sweep that reports a site it may not fix is complete; one that silently fixes across a boundary is not」), and this seat applied only the label needed to reach an inbox while ⛔ explicitly declining to grade.

### ⛔ Three fences, all carried

1. ⛔ **Do not take a `0` from `grep "refused a read on"` as absence.** Four fixtures repo-wide route refusals through `captureExpectedReadRefusals`, which **withholds the driver line**; on #17985's own lane that produced a clean zero over **two of five real sites**. For those sites, measure through the capture's own `refusals` counter. ⚠️ This is the single most likely way this card gets closed wrongly.
2. ⛔ **Do not silence, filter or re-level the log line.** The count must fall because the read **succeeds** — proven positively with a one-off assertion printing the rows now returned, restored under a `trap` and verified by `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob. Precedent: PR #17982, PR #18067.
3. ⛔ **Register objects LOCALLY**, only the columns the reading path touches ⇒ ⛔ no dependency edge onto `plugin-auth` / `plugin-security`.

### ⚠️ The `runtime` half is the harder one and must not be mistaken for the easier one

`@objectstack/client`'s 227 are **visible in the log** and the completeness is proven (the seven files sum to the whole-package count ⇒ no eighth site).

⭐ `@objectstack/runtime`'s two are different in kind: they **declare `ABSENT_AUTHZ_TABLES` and assert the withheld counts**. ⇒ the false green there is **defended by a passing test**. Fixing it means deleting an assertion that currently passes, which will look like removing coverage unless the PR says plainly that the assertion was pinning the symptom rather than the behaviour. ⚠️ Expect that to be the review's sticking point.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — the edits are fixture registrations; the judgement is 「which zeros are real」, and the `runtime` pair needs an argument, not just a diff.

### ⚠️ One correction to the card, so the dev does not lose time on it

The card names `resolve-authz-context.ts` without a path. Its source neighbourhood on `main` is **`packages/core/src/security/`** — which is **`domain:engine`**, ⛔ not this lane. This is ⛔ **not** an invitation to edit it: the card's own remedy is to register the objects **LOCALLY in the fixtures**, and precedent PR #18067 landed that with **0 product code touched**. If the delivery finds it cannot close a refused read without editing `packages/core`, that is a **stop-and-report**, ⛔ not a widening.

⛔ And the standing red line, carried explicitly because omitting it cost PR #17718 a hold and a re-route: **凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位,不论谁需要它** (`SKILL.md:231` · `core-rules.md:62` · `SKILL.md:287` · `lanes/cli.md:12` · `lanes/spec.md:12` · `dispatch-runbook.md:158`).

## ACCEPT — PR #18082

Reviewed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), session `session_01TbSMtGzMrtPwh925wDEZd5`, R74, **2026-09-14T00:0xZ**. 复核对 GitHub 与树核验,⛔ 不对报告的自述核验 — every reading below was taken by this seat, ⛔ not lifted from the report.

### Checklist conclusion

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | **draft**, base `main`, first body line `Fixes #18070` ✅ |
| closing-keyword whole-body scan | **only** `Fixes #18070`. The other three numbers in the body (#10629, #11081, #18067) carry **no** closing verb ⇒ ⛔ no foreign card can be auto-closed |
| file surface | **9 files, every one `*.test.ts`, NON-TEST = NONE** — exactly the declared surface, ⛔ no breach. `content/docs/releases/` untouched |
| no product code | ✅ confirmed from the file list, ⛔ not from the claim |
| changeset | **`skip-changeset` correct.** Both packages are published (`private` absent) but `files[]` = `['dist','README.md','CHANGELOG.md']` ⇒ `src/**/*.test.ts` ships nothing. This repo's form is the label, ⛔ not an empty changeset |
| CI, pinned to head `c19db3b67` | **52 check runs, every one on that head: 39 `success` + 13 `skipped`, ZERO non-success.** Both required floors — `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` — `completed`/`success` |
| governed faces | **NONE** ⇒ ordinary landing path, ⛔ not the four-part terminal path |
| diff totals | `9 files changed, 1047 insertions(+), 99 deletions(-)` against **current** `origin/main` — matches the report's totals exactly |

### The sticking point the report named, checked and cleared

The report flagged the two moved `silentChannels` pins as the review's crux. It is the right thing to have flagged, and it holds:

**`ABSENT_AUTHZ_TABLES` shrank 6 → `['sys_setting']`**, and `ALWAYS_READ_AUTHZ_TABLES` is gone. The old assertion required the five reads to keep being **REFUSED**. The replacement is:

```ts
const expectResolverAuthzReadsSucceed = async (): Promise<void> => {
  const data = kernel.getService<IDataEngine>('data');
  for (const table of PROVISIONED_AUTHZ_TABLES) {
    await expect(data.find(table, { where: {} })).resolves.toEqual([]);
  }
};
```

⭐ **`toEqual([])` reads as vacuous and is not**, and this is the reading that decides the review. The card's own mechanism is that a **missing** table answers `[]` — but that tolerance lives in `tryFind`, the resolver's per-read helper. This assertion calls **`data.find` directly**, and `find` **rejects** for an unregistered object — pinned independently on `main` at `packages/objectql/src/engine.test.ts:229` (`await expect(engine.find('old_data', {})).rejects.toThrow(…)`). ⇒ the assertion is red when the table is missing, red when rows exist (the report's own probe hit exactly that: `expected [ { id: probe-user } ] to deeply equal []`), and green only in the intended state — table present, state genuinely empty.

⇒ **The pin was turned around, ⛔ not deleted**: what it asserted — *"these five reads really happen on this path"* — is still asserted, in the direction the fix runs. **Call-site parity holds** (3 real call sites in `notifications.hono`, matching `main`'s 3; the conformance file gains sites). ⭐ And shrinking the declared set makes a regression **loud as well as red**, because `captureDriver` forwards an UNRECOGNISED refusal to `console.warn` — while the five were declared, the same regression was withheld and merely counted.

### Instrument discipline — the fence that mattered was honoured empirically

⭐ The log-grep fence was **not taken on trust**: `grep -c 'refused a read on'` over a full run of each runtime file reads a clean **0** while the capture's own `refusals` counter reads **52** and **63**. Both runtime numbers were taken from the counter, which is the only instrument that can see them. ⇒ the under-reading instrument the triage comment warned about (`5655984888`, fence 1) did not produce a single number in this delivery.

All eight of the card's client counts were re-derived and **none moved** (95/35/25/25/21/20/6, summing to 227); after, resolver-class is **0** in all nine sites. The 37 residual client refusals and the 2/3 residual `sys_setting` withholdings are **non-resolver classes** and are correctly left alone.

### Recorded, ⛔ not grounds for REWORK

- **Three gates were non-zero on first attempt for reasons outside the diff**, and the re-runs are declared: `check:type-check-debt` OOMed at `--max-old-space-size=4096` (its own text: *"NOT a pass and NOT a finding"*) and passed at 8192 — **raising the heap is the declared deviation**; `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` returned PREREQUISITE NOT MET before any `dist` existed and passed after `pnpm build`.
- **`origin/main` moved mid-run** (`fb29f62ce` → `c54d8d67b`). The dev merged via `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` and **re-ran the entire 52-gate union, both package suites, typecheck and the full `pnpm lint` at the post-merge HEAD** — the right order, and the BEFORE numbers are correctly pinned to `fb29f62ce` and labelled as such.
- ⚠️ **Per-file line counts in the report differ slightly from GitHub's** (schema-conformance reported `+184/-36` vs `+182/-38`; hono `+177/-63` vs `+179/-61`) while the **totals match exactly**. Immaterial, and recorded rather than waved past: a per-file split computed at a different moment than the one published is a reading that has drifted from its ref.
- `mcp_calls: 0` — the whole run went through repo-scoped REST after a green probe. ⛔ No git-answerable question was put to the API.

### Out-of-scope findings — verified, and one carrier corrected

Both were reported `noted, not filed`. The first (37 residual non-resolver client refusals plus the residual `sys_setting` withholdings) names its carrier as *"whoever picks up that class, which lands in these same files"* — a real, nameable follow-up, so the fallback holds. The second (`expected-read-refusal-noise.ts` prescribes the repair for *"a table that started resolving"* but offers no affordance for asserting the **success** that replaces the refusal, so each consumer hand-rolls it — written twice in this PR) declares **`Carrier: none`**, and is correctly outside the three filing classes: a design observation about a test helper is neither a reproducible defect nor a contract violation. ⇒ ⛔ no card filed for it, and ⛔ it is not silently dropped either — it is recorded here.

A `pull_request.closed` event arrived claiming `outcome: merged`. ⛔ That is a relayed claim, not a reading — this repo has answered `merged: false` and even **omitted** the field while the change was already on `main`, and `auto_merge` reads null after a *successful* enqueue. **Landing commit**, taken from the tree (`git log -1 origin/main -- packages/runtime/src/notifications.hono.integration.test.ts`):

```

```

All nine files are present in that commit, and the totals match the reviewed diff byte-for-byte in count.

### Residue stripped by hand — the **fifth** instance of this class

The PR carried `Fixes`, so the card auto-closed `completed`. ⛔ The `pm:*` state and the assignee did **not** leave with it:

```
after auto-close   labels: bug · domain:cli · pm:dispatched · priority:p2 · tests
                   assignees: os-warren
after strip        labels: bug · domain:cli · priority:p2 · tests
                   assignees: (none)                    read back, CLEAN
```

Stripped with a **targeted single-label DELETE** plus a targeted assignee DELETE, ⛔ never a whole-set replace on a closed card, and read back afterwards because an HTTP 200 is not a landing. Grading and routing labels (`bug`, `domain:cli`, `priority:p2`, `tests`) are deliberately preserved — 归属不是状态.

⚠️ The previous shift hand-cleared this same residue **four** times in one day and recorded that 「四比四 ⛔ 不是巧合」. This is instance **five**, on a different shift and a different account ⇒ recorded here as further evidence for **#14881**, which is the card that owns the theme.

### ⭐ One platform reading this landing produced

The landing commit's committer date is **00:23:44Z** — **one second BEFORE** the `added_to_merge_queue` event at 00:23:45Z. ⇒ the commit is created when the **queue branch is built**, not when it merges, so its timestamp dates the *enqueue*, ⛔ not the landing. Anyone reconstructing a landing window from commit dates will be off by the whole queue dwell time (here ~28 minutes). The queue ref that carried it, `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-18082-57343f761…`, produced sha `b3d6918b86…`, and the PR stacked behind it (#18046) was speculatively built **on that sha** — which is why the remaining queue ref now reads `pr-18046-b3d6918b86…` with `b3d6918b86` being plain `main`.

⇒ Subscription closed; this seat is unsubscribed from PR #18082. Nothing further is owed on this card.
